W01_lookup.description: one person by id (no property index: label scan + filter)
W01_lookup.query: MATCH (p:Person {id: 'p4573'}) RETURN p.name AS name, p.age AS age
W01_lookup.sql: SELECT name, age FROM person WHERE id = 'p4573'

W03a_filter_selective.query: MATCH (p:Person) WHERE p.age = 42 AND p.score > 0.9 RETURN p.id AS id
W03a_filter_selective.sql: SELECT id FROM person WHERE age = 42 AND score > 0.9

W03b_filter_broad_count.query: MATCH (p:Person) WHERE p.age < 60 AND p.active = true RETURN count(p) AS n
W03b_filter_broad_count.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM person WHERE age < 60 AND active = 1

W03c_filter_broad_rows.query: MATCH (p:Person) WHERE p.age < 60 RETURN p.id AS id
W03c_filter_broad_rows.sql: SELECT id FROM person WHERE age < 60

W04a_hop_typical.sql: SELECT dst FROM knows WHERE src = 'p3052'

W04b_hop_hub.sql: SELECT dst FROM knows WHERE src = 'p0'

W05a_two_hop_distinct.description: distinct friends-of-friends of a typical person
W05a_two_hop_distinct.query: MATCH (p:Person {id: 'p3052'})-[:KNOWS]->(:Person)-[:KNOWS]->(f:Person) RETURN DISTINCT f.id AS id
W05a_two_hop_distinct.sql: SELECT DISTINCT k2.dst FROM knows k1 JOIN knows k2 ON k2.src = k1.dst WHERE k1.src = 'p3052'

W05b_three_hop_count.description: distinct people exactly three KNOWS hops away
W05b_three_hop_count.query: MATCH (p:Person {id: 'p3052'})-[:KNOWS]->(:Person)-[:KNOWS]->(:Person)-[:KNOWS]->(f:Person) RETURN count(DISTINCT f) AS n

W06a_var_len_1_3.query: MATCH (p:Person {id: 'p3052'})-[:KNOWS*1..3]->(f:Person) RETURN count(DISTINCT f) AS n
W06a_var_len_1_3.sql: WITH RECURSIVE r(n, d) AS (SELECT dst, 1 FROM knows WHERE src = 'p3052' UNION SELECT k.dst, r.d + 1 FROM r JOIN knows k ON k.src = r.n WHERE r.d < 3) SELECT count(DISTINCT n) FROM r

W06b_var_len_unbounded.description: every ancestor of a leaf company
W06b_var_len_unbounded.sql: WITH RECURSIVE a(id) AS (SELECT parent FROM company WHERE id = 'c832' UNION SELECT c.parent FROM a JOIN company c ON c.id = a.id WHERE c.parent IS NOT NULL) SELECT id FROM a WHERE id IS NOT NULL

W07a_join_coworkers.description: co-workers of a typical person (two comma patterns)
W07a_join_coworkers.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM works_at w1 JOIN works_at w2 ON w2.company = w1.company WHERE w1.person = 'p3052' AND w2.person <> w1.person

W07b_join_full_graph.description: people who live in the city their employer is in (three patterns over the whole graph)
W07b_join_full_graph.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM works_at w JOIN person p ON p.id = w.person JOIN company c ON c.id = w.company WHERE p.city = c.city

W08a_group_industry.description: employees and mean age per industry
W08a_group_industry.query: MATCH (p:Person)-[:WORKS_AT]->(c:Company) RETURN c.industry AS industry, count(p) AS n, avg(p.age) AS avg_age ORDER BY industry ASC
W08a_group_industry.sql: SELECT c.industry, count(*), avg(p.age) FROM works_at w JOIN person p ON p.id = w.person JOIN company c ON c.id = w.company GROUP BY c.industry ORDER BY c.industry

W08b_group_city_top5.description: five most populous cities (tie-broken by id)
W08b_group_city_top5.query: MATCH (p:Person)-[:LIVES_IN]->(x:City) RETURN x.id AS city, count(p) AS n ORDER BY n DESC, city ASC LIMIT 5
W08b_group_city_top5.sql: SELECT city, count(*) AS n FROM person GROUP BY city ORDER BY n DESC, city ASC LIMIT 5

W09_sort_limit.description: top 10 people by score (scores are unique)
W09_sort_limit.query: MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p.id AS id, p.score AS score ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 10
W09_sort_limit.sql: SELECT id, score FROM person ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 10

W10a_exists.query: MATCH (c:Company) WHERE EXISTS { (c)<-[:WORKS_AT]-(:Person {age: 25}) } RETURN count(c) AS n
W10a_exists.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM company c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM works_at w JOIN person p ON p.id = w.person WHERE w.company = c.id AND p.age = 25)

W10b_not_exists.description: people who know nobody (negated pattern predicate)
W10b_not_exists.query: MATCH (p:Person) WHERE NOT (p)-[:KNOWS]->(:Person) RETURN count(p) AS n
W10b_not_exists.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM person p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM knows k WHERE k.src = p.id)

W11a_at_least.description: people who know at least 20 people (typed plan)
W11a_at_least.sql: SELECT src FROM knows GROUP BY src HAVING count(*) >= 20

W11b_all.description: companies whose every parent shares their industry (vacuously true for roots; typed plan)
W11b_all.sql: SELECT c.id FROM company c LEFT JOIN company p ON p.id = c.parent WHERE c.parent IS NULL OR p.industry = c.industry

W13_transitive_inference.description: derive every indirect SUBSIDIARY_OF pair with InferenceEngine (whole graph as facts)
W13_transitive_inference.sql: WITH RECURSIVE a(c, anc, d) AS (SELECT id, parent, 1 FROM company WHERE parent IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT a.c, p.parent, a.d + 1 FROM a JOIN company p ON p.id = a.anc WHERE p.parent IS NOT NULL) SELECT count(*) FROM a WHERE d >= 2

W14b_derived_via_var_len.description: the same answer with a variable-length path on the base graph
W14b_derived_via_var_len.query: MATCH (c:Company {id: 'c832'})-[:SUBSIDIARY_OF*]->(r:Company) WHERE NOT (r)-[:SUBSIDIARY_OF]->(:Company) RETURN r.id AS id

W14a_derived_query.description: ultimate parent of a leaf company over materialized SUBSIDIARY_OF edges
W14a_derived_query.query: MATCH (c:Company {id: 'c832'})-[:SUBSIDIARY_OF]->(r:Company) WHERE NOT (r)-[:SUBSIDIARY_OF]->(:Company) RETURN r.id AS id
